reviews.author: Cesar Ramirez
reviews.excerpt: Write 100 words about
reviews.review:
Write 100 words about
"Let Yourself Go"
This is a Disco mix I did back in 2001 that was originally recorded onto a cassette and recently digitized by a friend of mine. The mix is made up of various Disco tracks that were made popular in Chicago's underground scene by the likes of Ron Hardy, Frankie Knuckles, and many other DJ's in Chicago during the late 1970's and all throughout the 1980's. Both Ron & Frankie were major influences on myself and many other DJ's. I was fortunate to have learned about they're musical selection and style by listening to a set of tapes that were given to me by a good friend during '96-'98. It's a variety of Soulful, Funky, and Garage Disco. It also features a edit of "Love Hangover" by Diana Ross done by none other than Ron Hardy himself! I enjoy this mix very much and am happy to have it available on a digital format. I hope everyone who takes a listen will enjoy it as well!

A weekly series on their Instagram page where guest artists select 5 tracks that jack, to promote. 
The mix includes tracks from that series and, tracks from Viva Acids first 12" release. The first track/mix is one of those tracks mixed with an old Richie Hawtin track!
Bai-ee's track selection also features a blend of classic Acid House tracks from the genre's pioneers alongside contemporary cuts that push the sound into new territories. A highly recommended mix to listen to for fans of the Acid House genre!

reviews.title: Brutus
reviews.author: Cesar Ramirez
reviews.excerpt: Chicago native Specter and his very unique release on Theo Parrish's Sound Signature label. It's a double album tribute to his dog, best friend, and very much like a son, Brutus. There are a few…
reviews.review:
Chicago native Specter and his very unique release on Theo Parrish's Sound Signature label. It's a double album tribute to his dog, best friend, and very much like a son, Brutus. There are a few things that make this album very unique. It is a concept album which is something you don't see much in House Music or Electronic Dance Music in general. Specter expresses his love for Brutus in a special and musical way. Each track tells a story about the life of Brutus. For example, the opening track "The Birth" is an introduction to the life of Brutus that features a bassline which is the driving force of the track. This track has no kick in it. It is layered with Jazzy like chords along with synth riffs that make the track very interesting. The next track "The Spirit" is very much a spiritual expression that features percussion in a tribal way with some quirky synth sounds and very deep & jazzy chords. The 3rd track titled "The Death" you can feel a mix of emotions associated with sadness & loss. Overall this track is a beautiful piece of music in which Specter expresses how he felt right before and when Brutus' life came to an end. A very nice composition for those who enjoy playing instrumental tracks that speak volumes.
The 4th and final track "The Ascension" describes how Specter felt once he knew that his companion(Brutus) was in a better place and no longer suffering. The album as a whole is an emotional & heartfelt tribute to Brutus which was executed in a remarkable manner and style that only Specter could have done!

reviews.review:
From the vaults of the Soul Foundation Chicago archives comes a gem that resonates with the raw spirit of underground dance culture! A mix by none other than Traxx (Nation/Dirty Criminals). Recently unearthed and digitized from a cassette tape, this is a slice of electronic history that transports the listener straight back to the 1990s, an era when house music was expanding its boundaries and setting dance floors ablaze.
The A-side is pure dynamite. Deep House grooves blend seamlessly with elements of Minimal Techno and Detroit Beatdown, creating a sonic landscape that is as hypnotic as it is uplifting. Each track flows into the next with a relentless energy, building momentum with every beat, yet never sacrificing the depth that defines Traxx’s signature style. It’s an ode to the dancefloor, where rhythm reigns supreme and the crowd moves as one collective pulse.
Flip to the B-side, and the tempo shifts. Traxx takes us on a deeper journey, slowing things down just enough to let the intricacies of his selections breathe. But make no mistake—this isn’t a comedown, it’s a masterclass in groove control. The beats still bang with precision, the vibe is still thick, but there’s a more introspective energy at play. It’s a side that commands attention, revealing the layers of house and techno’s more subdued, yet equally powerful, facets.

This rare recording captures Kenny "Jammin" Jason, an original member of the Hot Mix 5, mixing live on Chicago’s legendary 102.7 WBMX radio station back in 1986! Every Saturday night, the Hot Mix 5 DJs brought the airwaves to life with live sets, blending the freshest underground Chicago House Music with vibrant Italo Disco tracks.
The mix begins with the radio host introducing Kenny "Jammin" Jason before the music takes center stage. Throughout the set, you’ll hear periodic reminders from the host, letting listeners know they’re tuned in to 102.7 WBMX—a nostalgic touch that adds to the authentic experience.
Preserving mixes like this is vital for Chicago House history, and we’re thrilled to have this one in our archives. It’s more than just a mix; it’s a time capsule from a pivotal era in dance music.
Take a journey back in time and lose yourself in the sounds of Chicago's own Kenny "Jammin" Jason. Don’t miss it—check it out!

reviews.review:
UnderGround Existence presents another timeless mix from the legendary Hotmix 5 Chicago DJ, Julian "Jumpin" Perez! This classic recording from 1985 is a two-part mix featuring sets originally captured on cassette tapes. Nearly 20 years later, these sets were digitized and compiled into a single file, now available as an approximately 1-hour and 12-minute journey of Julian's live radio magic.
In this mix, Julian showcases his impressive DJ skills, including live sampling, editing, scratching, and cutting. He masterfully uses two copies of the same record to create seamless back-and-forth transitions—a hallmark style of 1980s DJing!
The track selection spans music from 1979-1985, featuring an eclectic blend of Italo Disco, Boogie, Electro, Disco Funk, and even some left-field gems like the iconic "Optimo" by Liquid Liquid, a staple in Chicago's underground scene.
Whether you're cruising down Lake Shore Drive or relaxing at home, this mix offers the perfect soundtrack. Don't miss this incredible piece of musical history!

reviews.title: Let's Drop (Deep House Mix)
reviews.author: Cesar Ramirez
reviews.excerpt: Deep House aficionado and Windy City native, DJ Stephen P, delivers a masterful mix that has stood the test of time. Recorded at the Campsite Lab in Chicago in 2001, this set is a shining example of…
reviews.review:
Deep House aficionado and Windy City native, DJ Stephen P, delivers a masterful mix that has stood the test of time. Recorded at the Campsite Lab in Chicago in 2001, this set is a shining example of the soulful, groove-heavy sound that defined the era—and still resonates today.
From the very first track, Stephen P sets a warm, immersive tone. A steady, hypnotic beat, accented by jazzy keys and lush vocal samples, pulls listeners into an effortless rhythm, creating a sonic space that feels as inviting as it does energizing. His transitions are smooth yet dynamic, artfully blending classic Deep House elements with subtle, tech-infused grooves that keep the momentum alive.
What’s remarkable about this mix is its timeless quality. Nearly 25 years later, the tracks still sound fresh and relevant. The selection features music by some of the genre’s most iconic producers, including Vincenzo, Inland Knights, Sandy Rivera, Tony Senghore, Furry Freaks, Pete Moss, To-Ka Project, and more. Each track is a testament to the enduring appeal of Deep House, showcasing intricate melodies, rolling basslines, and an undeniable sense of soul.
Stephen P’s ability to curate and seamlessly blend these tracks highlights his skill as both a DJ and storyteller. Whether you’re revisiting this mix or discovering it for the first time, it’s a must-hear for fans of Deep House and Chicago’s rich musical legacy. Check it!

reviews.title: Live @ Viva Acid Closing Party, Chicago 10-6-2024
reviews.author: Cesar Ramirez
reviews.excerpt: Bai-ee delivered a standout performance with a mix recorded on October 6th, 2024, for Viva Acid's closing party at Chicago's Podlasie Nightclub. The set kicked off with a sleek, minimal Acid track,…
reviews.review:
Bai-ee delivered a standout performance with a mix recorded on October 6th, 2024, for Viva Acid's closing party at Chicago's Podlasie Nightclub. The set kicked off with a sleek, minimal Acid track, setting the tone for an unforgettable journey. From there, he transitioned into a few cuts reminiscent of late 1980s New Wave, evoking a sense of nostalgia with a modern edge.
As the night progressed, Bai-ee shifted gears into an electro-jazzy-funk vibe, skillfully weaving through various shades of Deep House. True to his roots, he ensured the mix was packed with driving Acid basslines and early Chicago-style drum beats—a fitting tribute to the city’s iconic House music legacy. 
One of the night’s highlights came as Bai-ee layered Donna Summer's "I Feel Love" over a banging Acid track, creating a moment of pure dancefloor euphoria! He followed this with a stunning instrumental remake of "Glowing In The Dark," a cherished Chicago underground Synth-Pop/New Wave classic from the '80s. Bai-ee wrapped up his set with yet another pulsating Acid track, leaving the crowd energized and wanting more!
With nearly 30 years of experience behind the decks, Bai-ee continues to honor Chicago's rich underground dance music heritage, proving once again why he remains a vital force in the scene! Check this mix out!
